tasks.short: Signal and assist loading or unloading workers

steps.what: Signal other workers during actual loading or unloading
Provide the actual physical assistance needed for loading or unloading

tasks.design: Keep live signalling and physical assistance with the operator. A loading checklist or native job view cannot replace either activity, and this task does not establish a separate operator-owned shipping record.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work responds to actual moving loads and workers rather than a digital queue.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software capability removes the actual physical or signalling work.
tasks.still_hard: Changing load positions and coordination with people in the work area.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise the actual scene and communicate immediately.
tasks.altitude: No change to the operator's role.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: load signalling and physical assistance are live work; warehouse record automation does not perform them.

assumptions: Shares are provisional focal-role physical work, excluding other workers' labour and hoist runtime. Signals and assistance may interleave; shares describe their actual labour components.
The actual scene and workers produce the live inputs. No structured load-status input is assumed to exist for a machine.

Record, report and send boundaries were inspected before zero. The task assigns signalling and assistance, not order confirmation, tally writing or shipping paperwork. No trailing activity record is invented. If the operator actually owns a scan, tally or handoff record, add that observed action and assess the native loading form before confirming zero.
A native job view or checklist is assessed but cannot substitute for the counted live work. Live signals are the human activity itself, not an uncounted electronic send.
No new implementation or recurring upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Whether this operator also performs a required loading scan or tally
research_questions: Observe a loading cycle and separate any real operator-owned record action from signalling and assistance.

incremental.description: No new automation or recurring upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All 40 signalling and 60 assistance points remain. A congested loading cycle retains more live coordination rather than creating a software saving; no unobserved tally duty is added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe gauges and signals to verify load positions

steps.what: Observe actual hoist gauges and indicators
Observe workers' hand signals and verify the actual load position or depth

tasks.design: Retain actual gauge observation and interpretation of workers' hand signals. A native display may already show position or depth, but its existing calculation and display runtime is not human labour removed by a new design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verification depends on combining instrument indications with the actual scene and signals.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing indicators support observation without replacing verification.
tasks.still_hard: Disagreement between an indication, a signal and the observed load.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise ambiguity and seek human clarification before relying on an indication.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: actual gauge and hand-signal observation remains human even where equipment already displays calculated position.

assumptions: Provisional shares cover verification only, not a new autonomous hoist controller. Existing sensing and display runtime earn no saving.
Gauges and actual workers produce the inputs during observation. The graph assumes no machine-readable hand-signal or verified-position record.

Before zero, record/lookup/send boundaries were considered. This task does not assign a position report or secondary log; the observed verification is the output. A native view or template cannot replace the actual observation. Any actual required depth entry or completion send must be separately added and assessed before confirming this estimate.
No implementation or recurring upkeep is proposed.
unknowns: Whether the actual operation requires a separate depth or position entry
research_questions: Is there a real manual position record beyond the existing equipment display?

incremental.description: No new automation or recurring upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Retain all 60 observation and 40 verification points. An obscured load or ambiguous hand signal retains human clarification; display runtime and a fictional log provide no saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select loads by weight and size specifications

steps.what: Read load specifications and verify available inventory references
Compare recorded load weights and dimensions against the specified limits
Inspect candidate loads and select the actual suitable material

tasks.design: In a warehouse with existing load records, test native weight and dimension filters in the stock module of {OPS_SYSTEM}. Produce candidates only; retain full specification reading, record verification and physical selection, without issuing a lift instruction or creating a new selection log.
tasks.previous_blocker: Line-by-line comparisons of recorded weight and dimensions can precede physical selection.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exact numeric filters over existing load records.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the physical load matches its tag and is suitable under the actual conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Identify a physical mismatch that an inventory filter cannot resolve.
tasks.altitude: Less numeric comparison, with physical selection responsibility unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native inventory filters can compare recorded load weights and dimensions; physical suitability still needs inspection.

assumptions: Provisional shares describe an actual warehouse workflow with recorded loads and manual numeric comparison. This is a scenario to validate, not evidence that every hoist operator has such a baseline. Tag-only operations need a revised graph.

The existing receiving process produces load identifier, weight, dimensions, units and location; no new capture duty is transferred for free. s1 verifies these against the required limits. Missing dimensions or units are manually resolved within s1/s3, and unsupported loads are not automatically excluded as unsuitable.
Test native filters first. s2 removes the exact comparison of valid numeric records, not specification reading or physical selection. Existing automatic filtering and system runtime earn no saving.

Record and send boundaries are inspected: this task selects material, with no established separate confirmation record or lift authorisation. Do not add a trailing log. Any actual order confirmation must be separately assessed.
unknowns: Existence and completeness of recorded load weights and dimensions
Whether numeric filtering is already available and used
research_questions: Observe selection and verify both the manual comparison baseline and the producer of recorded weights and dimensions.

incremental.description: Maintain weight/dimension field and unit mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 20 numeric-comparison points less 0.8 upkeep gives 19.2. With mostly untagged or incomplete loads, retain manual identification and comparison; only 4 points of complete compatible records can be filtered, giving 3.2 net. Physical selection remains fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep live signalling and load verification human; use numeric filters only where real inventory records support them.
skills_to_grow: Check inventory units against physical load tags
role.ambitious_version: No expanded operating authority is justified; verified comparison savings can support closer physical checks.
